messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall-alex — GPU node gpu-node-17 is flapping drivers and we've observed 200+ Xid errors in the last 5m. Autoscaling triggered evictions. Please ack and triage.
oncall-alex: ACK — I'm on it, pulling logs now. Can someone confirm if this is single node or multi-node pattern?
infra-kyle: I'm seeing noisy ECC/Xid on node gpu-node-17 only. dmesg shows repeated entries. quick snippet:```
[ 245678.123456] NVRM: Xid (79, 0) 66ffff9a 0 00000000 00000000 00000000
[ 245678.123789] NVRM: GPU at 0000:87:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 245678.124000] kernel: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s
```
oncall-alex: that GPU falling off the bus explains container OOMs/crashes. Which pods were impacted?
infra-kyle: two inference deployments on that node experienced OOM SIGKILLs and runtime crashes: `redwood-gen-1` and `embeddings-v2`. kubelet logs show repeated `container runtime: container status error: SIGKILL` tied to GPU faults.
ops-liz: Customer telemetry — CS dashboard shows ~4.3% request error spike for customers in us-west-2, correlated to that node. cs-jordan: calling out that a production customer reported increased 5xxs.
oncall-alex: ok plan: cordon node, drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`, then either restart nvidia driver or reboot node depending on result. Any objections?
sre-maria: +1 to cordon/drain, don't reboot until we try driver recover. If driver unload fails, we'll reboot. Also enable debug logs during the window.
infra-kyle: attempting soft recover: `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` then `modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia`. Will paste output.
infra-kyle: run output:```
Stopping nvidia-persistenced.service: [ OK ]
modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia is in use.
modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'nvidia': Unknown symbol in module
```
oncall-alex: modprobe failed, looks like kernel-level fault. going to cordon and drain now. executing: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
ops-liz: initiating traffic mitigation — routing policy updated to divert new inference requests away from us-west-2 GPU pool for the next 30m. Console link: https://console.redwood.ai/projects/infra/traffic (shared)
cs-jordan: notifying impacted customers; will open bridge if we see >10% sustained errors. low-level notices already sent to two accounts.
infra-kyle: drain completed, evicted pods. Node still showing ECC/Xid noise in `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi -q` intermittent hangs. Last `nvidia-smi` returns `Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch`.
oncall-alex: since soft driver reload failed and NVML mismatch present, escalate to node reboot. scheduling a rolling reboot for gpu-node-17, will monitor post-boot. ETA 5m.
sre-maria: capture kernel and driver versions for postmortem: `uname -a` and `modinfo nvidia | grep version` — drop into the ticket.
infra-kyle: pre-reboot snapshot:
`uname -a`: Linux gpu-node-17 5.15.0-1087-aws #92 SMP x86_64 GNU/Linux
`modinfo nvidia | grep ^version`: version: 535.86.01
`/var/log/kern.log` shows repeated `NVRM: Xid (79` and `GPU has fallen off the bus`.
oncall-alex: rebooting node now via `sudo systemctl reboot` — will post back on boot and run validation.
incident-bot: system: node gpu-node-17 reboot initiated by oncall-alex.
ops-liz: continued mitigation — raising capacity on dedicated fallback pool to absorb load + keeping temporary routing.
infra-kyle: node came back up, nvidia driver probe successful, `nvidia-smi` returning GPUs health ok. quick `dmesg` post-boot still shows a few correctable ECC notices but no Xid surges.
sre-maria: starting canary: unschedule two least-critical pods onto node, observe for 10 minutes, then resume normal scheduling.
oncall-alex: canary pods started, running inference smoke tests. latency and error rate within expected thresholds.
cs-jordan: customer impact summary: brief spike in 5xxs affecting a small percentage of requests (peak 5% for 12min). No data loss reported. customers contacted and escalations opened.
sre-maria: next steps for postmortem: collect full kernel + driver logs, GPU telemetry, pod lifecycles; evaluate whether hardware swap required for GPU card on node-17; consider proactive cordon for similar telemetry pattern.
infra-kyle: filing HW ticket with datacenter to check GPU PCIe link and ECC counters. adding label `gpu:quarantine` to node for follow-up.
oncall-alex: handoff to @sre-maria for overnight follow-up. summary: Xid/ECC surge caused driver instability -> driver reload failed -> node reboot resolved transient state -> customers saw short error spike. If anything flares, call pager.
sre-maria: taking over — will consolidate logs and draft postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:
